metadata.title: FaBiO, the FRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology
metadata.description:
FaBiO, the FRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology, is an ontology for recording and publishing on the Semantic Web descriptions of entities that are published or potentially publishable, and that contain or are referred to by bibliographic references, or entities used to define such bibliographic references. FaBiO entities are primarily textual publications such as books, magazines, newspapers and journals, and items of their content such as poems, conference papers and editorials.  However, they also include blogs, web pages, datasets, computer algorithms, experimental protocols, formal specifications and vocabularies, legal records, governmental papers, technical and commercial reports and similar publications, and also anthologies, catalogues and similar collections. 

FaBiO classes are structured according to the FRBR schema of Works, Expressions, Manifestations and Items. Additional properties have been added to extends the FRBR data model by linking Works and Manifestations (fabio:hasManifestation and fabio:isManifestationOf), Works and Items (fabio:hasPortrayal and fabio:isPortrayedBy), and Expressions and Items  (fabio:hasRepresentation and fabio:isRepresentedBy).

classes.label: periodical
classes.definition: A publication issued on a regular and ongoing basis as a series of issues, each issue comprising separate periodical items, for example editorials, articles, news items and/or other writings.
classes.comment: A publication issued on a regular and ongoing basis as a series of issues, each issue comprising separate periodical items, for example editorials, articles, news items and/or other writings.

classes.label: moving image
classes.definition: A moving display, either generated dynamically by a computer program or formed from a series of pre-recorded still images imparting an impression of motion when shown in succession.  Examples include animations, cine films, videos, and computational simulations. Expressions of moving images may incorporate synchronized soundtracks.
classes.comment: A moving display, either generated dynamically by a computer program or formed from a series of pre-recorded still images imparting an impression of motion when shown in succession.  Examples include animations, cine films, videos, and computational simulations. Expressions of moving images may incorporate synchronized soundtracks.

classes.label: taxonomy
classes.definition: A classification arranged in a hierarchical structure of classes and subclasses, showing parent-child isA relationships, or broader_than - narrower_than relationships.
classes.comment: A classification arranged in a hierarchical structure of classes and subclasses, showing parent-child isA relationships, or broader_than - narrower_than relationships.

classes.label: vocabulary
classes.definition: A set of words, either constituting a language, or more specifically used to describe a particular domain of knowledge.
classes.comment: A set of words, either constituting a language, or more specifically used to describe a particular domain of knowledge.

classes.label: analog item
classes.definition: A real object that is an exemplar of a fabio:Manifestation, such as a particular copy of the book 'Alice's adventures in Wonderland', that a person may own.
classes.comment: A real object that is an exemplar of a fabio:Manifestation, such as a particular copy of the book 'Alice's adventures in Wonderland', that a person may own. | An analog item is an exemplar of an analog manifestation only and it is always stored in a storage medium suitable for analog objects, such as paper, vinyl discs and films.

classes.label: work
classes.definition: A subclass of FRBR work, restricted to works that are published or potentially publishable, and that contain or are referred to by bibliographic references, or entities used to define bibliographic references. FaBiO works, and their expressions and manifestations, are primarily textual publications such as books, magazines, newspapers and journals, and items of their content.  However, they also include datasets, computer algorithms, experimental protocols, formal specifications and vocabularies, legal records, governmental papers, technical and commercial reports and similar publications, and also bibliographies, reference lists, library catalogues and similar collections. For this reason, fabio:Work is not an equivalent class to frbr:ScholarlyWork.  An example of a fabio:Work is your latest research paper.
classes.comment: A subclass of FRBR work, restricted to works that are published or potentially publishable, and that contain or are referred to by bibliographic references, or entities used to define bibliographic references. FaBiO works, and their expressions and manifestations, are primarily textual publications such as books, magazines, newspapers and journals, and items of their content. An example of a fabio:Work is your latest research paper. | A fabio:Work can only have part or be part of another fabio:Work. Moreover, it can be realized only by fabio:Expression(s).

classes.label: press release
classes.definition: A news report published by an organization to provide information to journalists.
classes.comment: A news report published by an organization to provide information to journalists.

classes.label: laboratory notebook
classes.definition: A notebook used by an individual research scientist as the primary record of his or her research activities. A researcher may use a laboratory notebook to document hypotheses, to describe experiments and to record data in various formats, to provide details of data analysis and interpretation, or to record the validation or invalidation of the original hypotheses. The laboratory notebook serves as an organizational tool and a memory aid.  It may also have a role in recording and protecting any intellectual property created during the research, and may be used in evidence when establishing priority of discoveries, for example in patent applications.  Electronic versions of laboratory notebooks are increasingly being employed by researchers, particularly in chemistry and the pharmaceutical industry.

classes.label: news item
classes.definition: A published news report.
classes.comment: A published news report.

classes.label: web site
classes.definition: A collection of related web pages containing text, images, videos and/or other digital assets that are addressed relative to a common Uniform Resource Locator (URL). A web site is hosted on at least one web server, accessible via a network such as the Internet or a private local area network.
classes.comment: A collection of related web pages containing text, images, videos and/or other digital assets that are addressed relative to a common Uniform Resource Locator (URL). A web site is hosted on at least one web server, accessible via a network such as the Internet or a private local area network.

classes.label: anthology
classes.definition: A collection of selected literary or scholastics works, for example poems, short stories, plays or research papers.
classes.comment: A collection of selected literary or scholastics works, for example poems, short stories, plays or research papers.

classes.label: archival record set
classes.definition: A collection of archival records.
classes.comment: A collection of archival records.

classes.label: authority file
classes.definition: A controlled vocabulary or official list that establishes, for consistency, the authoritative forms of headings, and the preferred terms or proper names to be used, when creating a catalogue or when indexing and searching a set of entities within a defined domain.
classes.comment: A controlled vocabulary or official list that establishes, for consistency, the authoritative forms of headings, and the preferred terms or proper names to be used, when creating a catalogue or when indexing and searching a set of entities within a defined domain.

classes.label: item
classes.definition: A subclass of FRBR item, restricted to exemplars of fabio:Manifestations.  An example of a fabio:Item is a printed copy of a journal article on your desk, or a PDF file of that article that you purchased from a publisher and that now resides in digital form on your computer hard drive.
classes.comment: A subclass of FRBR item, restricted to exemplars of fabio:Manifestations.  An example of a fabio:Item is a printed copy of a journal article on your desk, or a PDF file of that article that you purchased from a publisher and that now resides in digital form on your computer hard drive.   | A fabio:Item can only have part or be part of another fabio:Item. Moreover, it can be an exemplar only of a fabio:Manifestation.

classes.label: biography
classes.definition: An account of the events, works and achievements, both personal and professional, of a person, either living or dead.
classes.comment: An account of the events, works and achievements, both personal and professional, of a person, either living or dead.

classes.label: thesis
classes.definition: A book authored by a student containing a formal presentations of research outputs submitted for examination in completion of a course of study at an institution of higher education, to fulfil the requirements for an academic degree.  Also know as a dissertation.  [For the alternative meaning of the word 'thesis', namely the formulation of a concept, hypothesis, idea, point of view or theory presented for review and/or discussion, use fabio:Proposition.]
classes.comment: A book authored by a student containing a formal presentations of research outputs submitted for examination in completion of a course of study at an institution of higher education, to fulfil the requirements for an academic degree.  Also know as a dissertation.  [For the alternative meaning of the word 'thesis', namely the formulation of a concept, hypothesis, idea, point of view or theory presented for review and/or discussion, use fabio:Proposition.]

classes.label: brief report
classes.definition: A brief report document.  This term may also be used synonymously with Rapid Communication to mean 'A short rapidly published research article or conference paper, typically reporting significant research results that have been recently discovered, or a brief news item reporting such discoveries.'
classes.comment: A brief report document.  This term may also be used synonymously with Rapid Communication to mean 'A short rapidly published research article or conference paper, typically reporting significant research results that have been recently discovered, or a brief news item reporting such discoveries.'

classes.label: data management policy
classes.definition: A policy that descibes and defines how data should be managed, preserved and shared.
classes.comment: A policy that descibes and defines how data should be managed, preserved and shared.

classes.label: data file
classes.definition: A realisation of a fabio:Dataset (a frbr:Work) containing a defined collection of data with specific content and possibly with a specific version number, that can be embodied as a fabio:Digital Manifestation (a frbr:Manifestation with a specific format) and be represented by a specific fabio:ComputerFile (a frbr:Item) on someone's hard drive.
classes.comment: A realisation of a fabio:Dataset (a frbr:Work) containing a defined collection of data with specific content and possibly with a specific version number, that can be embodied as a fabio:Digital Manifestation (a frbr:Manifestation with a specific format) and be represented by a specific fabio:ComputerFile (a frbr:Item) on someone's hard drive.

classes.label: journal volume
classes.definition: A particular published volume of a journal, comprising one or more journal issues.
classes.comment: A particular published volume of a journal, comprising one or more journal issues.

classes.label: reference entry
classes.definition: A particular reference entry containing authoritative factual information on a certain topic, usually contained in a larger expression.
classes.comment: A particular reference entry containing authoritative factual information on a certain topic, usually contained in a larger expression.

classes.label: novel
classes.definition: A long fictitious narrative written in literary prose.
classes.comment: A long fictitious narrative written in literary prose.

classes.label: product review
classes.definition: A written review and critical analysis of the purpose, features, performance and other qualities of a product.
classes.comment: A written review and critical analysis of the purpose, features, performance and other qualities of a product.

classes.label: report
classes.definition: A formal factual, methodological, statistical, technical or research report issued by an individual, group, agency, government body or other institution.
classes.comment: A formal factual, methodological, statistical, technical or research report issued by an individual, group, agency, government body or other institution.

classes.label: patent application document
classes.definition: The physical or electronic realization of a patent application.
classes.comment: The physical or electronic realization of a patent application.

classes.label: patent application
classes.definition: A formal disclosure of a new invention, made in application for a patent.
classes.comment: A formal disclosure of a new invention, made in application for a patent.

classes.label: script
classes.definition: A small computer program written in a scripting language such as JavaScript, PHP or Perl that allows control of one or more software applications.
classes.comment: A small computer program written in a scripting language such as JavaScript, PHP or Perl that allows control of one or more software applications.

classes.label: relational database
classes.definition: A database in which the data are arranged in tables according to their common characteristics, with relationships between the tables being defined by a relational model or schema. A relational database is highly optimized for performance, and is queried using a database query language such as SQL (Structured Query Language).  The software used to create a relational database is called a relational database management system (RDBMS).
classes.comment: A database in which the data are arranged in tables according to their common characteristics, with relationships between the tables being defined by a relational model or schema. A relational database is highly optimized for performance, and is queried using a database query language such as SQL (Structured Query Language).  The software used to create a relational database is called a relational database management system (RDBMS).

classes.label: supplement
classes.definition: A supplement to a publication such as a book, journal, magazine or newspaper, additional to the main publication.  For example, a colour supplement to a sunday newspaper, or a special supplementary issue of a journal or a journal volume containing invited articles on a special topic, or abstracts or papers presented at a scientific conference.
classes.comment: A supplement to a publication such as a book, journal, magazine or newspaper, additional to the main publication.  For example, a colour supplement to a sunday newspaper, or a special supplementary issue of a journal or a journal volume containing invited articles on a special topic, or abstracts or papers presented at a scientific conference.

classes.label: diary
classes.definition: A personal record, in a form of book, with discrete entries (often handwritten) arranged by date, reporting what has happened over the course of a day or other period of time.
classes.comment: A personal record, in a form of book, with discrete entries (often handwritten) arranged by date, reporting what has happened over the course of a day or other period of time.

classes.label: ontology document
classes.definition: A document containing an ontology, for example an OWL (Web Ontology Language) file (http://www.w3.org/TR/owl-features/).
classes.comment: A document containing an ontology, for example an OWL (Web Ontology Language) file (http://www.w3.org/TR/owl-features/).

classes.label: quotation
classes.definition:
A passage of speech selected from a larger verbal or written expression for use in another expression, with specific attribution to its original source, and usually demarcated by quotation marks and / or by placing it in a separate indented paragraph. 

[Note: Use fabio:Quotation to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is a passage of speech, and fabio:Excerpt to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is not a passage of speech.]
classes.comment:
A passage of speech selected from a larger verbal or written expression for use in another expression, with specific attribution to its original source, and usually demarcated by quotation marks and / or by placing it in a separate indented paragraph. 

[Note: Use fabio:Quotation to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is a passage of speech, and fabio:Excerpt to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is not a passage of speech.] | A quotation is a repetition of what someone has said, and is presented "within quotation marks", for example:

On June 4th 1940, Winston Churchill made a speech on the radio that has since become famous, that included the words:
       " . . . we shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; we shall never surrender . . ."

Similarly, the words "but Brutus is an honourable man" from Mark Antony's funeral speech in Shakespeare's play Julius Caesar is a quotation, since Mark Antony says these words in the play.

classes.label: systematic review
classes.definition: A literature review focused on a single question that tries to identify, appraise, select and synthesize all high quality research evidence relevant to that question. Systematic reviews of high-quality randomized controlled trials are crucial to evidence-based medicine. An understanding of systematic reviews and how to implement them in practice is becoming mandatory for all professionals involved in the delivery of health care. Systematic reviews are not limited to medicine,  and are quite common in other sciences such as psychology, educational research and sociology.

classes.label: expression
classes.definition: A subclass of FRBR expression, restricted to expressions of fabio:Works.  For your latest research paper, the preprint submitted to the publisher, and the final published version to which the publisher assigned a unique digital object identifier, are both expressions of the same work.
classes.comment: A subclass of FRBR expression, restricted to expressions of fabio:Works. Moreover, it can be a representation only of a fabio:Work, and  it can be embodied only in fabio:Manifestation(s).

classes.label: notification of receipt
classes.definition: A notification of receipt of something, for example of receipt of a book that will later be the subject of a book review.
classes.comment: A notification of receipt of something, for example of receipt of a book that will later be the subject of a book review.

classes.label: minimal information standard
classes.definition: A metadata standard specifying items to be included when creating metadata describing a dataset of a particular type, or when creating a structured summary of the main findings of an article or report in a particular domain of interest, thereby ensuring adequate descriptive information is recorded for subsequent resource discovery and/or interpretation of the information described.  [See also fabio:ReportingStandard.]
classes.comment: A metadata standard specifying items to be included when creating metadata describing a dataset of a particular type, or when creating a structured summary of the main findings of an article or report in a particular domain of interest, thereby ensuring adequate descriptive information is recorded for subsequent resource discovery and/or interpretation of the information described.  [See also fabio:ReportingStandard.]

classes.label: chapter
classes.definition: A defined document section, forming part of or intended for inclusion within a larger document, usually with its own title or chapter number.  Different chapters within a document such as a book or a report may each be independently authored, or may all be authored by a single individual or group of authors.
classes.comment: A defined document section, forming part of or intended for inclusion within a larger document, usually with its own title or chapter number.  Different chapters within a document such as a book or a report may each be independently authored, or may all be authored by a single individual or group of authors.

classes.label: metadata
classes.definition: A separate work that provides information describing one or more characteristics of a resource or entity.
classes.comment: A separate work that provides information describing one or more characteristics of a resource or entity.

classes.label: concept
classes.definition:
A SKOS concept can be viewed as an idea or notion; a unit of thought. However, what constitutes a unit of thought is subjective, and this definition is meant to be suggestive, rather than restrictive.

The notion of a SKOS concept is useful when describing the conceptual or intellectual structure of a knowledge organization system, and when referring to specific ideas or meanings established within a KOS.

Note that, because SKOS is designed to be a vehicle for representing semi-formal KOS, such as thesauri and classification schemes, a certain amount of flexibility has been built in to the formal definition of this class.

classes.label: table
classes.definition: A graphical means of presenting data in a grid of rows and columns, within which the cells usually contain alphanumeric text or numeric values.  If included within a publication, a table typically appearing unaligned with the main body of text, with its own descriptive title.
classes.comment: A graphical means of presenting data in a grid of rows and columns, within which the cells usually contain alphanumeric text or numeric values.  If included within a publication, a table typically appearing unaligned with the main body of text, with its own descriptive title.

classes.label: meeting report
classes.definition: A report of a meeting of some kind.
classes.comment: A report of a meeting of some kind.

classes.label: clinical trial design
classes.definition: A predefined written procedural method, designed to ensure reliability of findings, for undertaking a medical or veterinary clinical study of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic or prophylactic drugs or treatments, or of devices or techniques, involving a randomized controlled trial for evidence-based assessment in humans or animals, specifying criteria of eligibility, nature of controls, sampling schedules, data collection parameters, statistical analyses, reporting standards, etc. to be employed in undertaking the clinical trial.
classes.comment: A predefined written procedural method, designed to ensure reliability of findings, for undertaking a medical or veterinary clinical study of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic or prophylactic drugs or treatments, or of devices or techniques, involving a randomized controlled trial for evidence-based assessment in humans or animals, specifying criteria of eligibility, nature of controls, sampling schedules, data collection parameters, statistical analyses, reporting standards, etc. to be employed in undertaking the clinical trial.

classes.label: application profile
classes.definition: A set of metadata elements, policies and guidelines defined for a particular application.  The metadata elements used in the application profile may be drawn from more than one element sets, including locally defined sets.
classes.comment: A set of metadata elements, policies and guidelines defined for a particular application.  The metadata elements used in the application profile may be drawn from more than one element sets, including locally defined sets.

classes.label: microblog
classes.definition: A social networking publication medium such as Twitter, Tumblr, FriendFeed, Facebook or MySpace. A microblog differs from a traditional blog in that its individual content items are smaller than a traditional blog posts, typically containing just a short sentence, a single image, or a URI.  These small messages are referred to as microposts.
classes.comment: A social networking publication medium such as Twitter, Tumblr, FriendFeed, Facebook or MySpace. A microblog differs from a traditional blog in that its individual content items are smaller than a traditional blog posts, typically containing just a short sentence, a single image, or a URI.  These small messages are referred to as microposts.

classes.label: movie
classes.definition: The realization of a moving image.
classes.comment: The realization of a moving image.

classes.label: standard operating procedure
classes.definition: Clear and detailed written instructions of a prescribed step-by-step procedure to be routinely followed, and decisions to be made when undertaking a specific task, process or function, to achieve consistent performance, ensure safety and/or assure data quality.  (Commonly abbreviated 'SOP'.)
classes.comment: Clear and detailed written instructions of a prescribed step-by-step procedure to be routinely followed, and decisions to be made when undertaking a specific task, process or function, to achieve consistent performance, ensure safety and/or assure data quality.  (Commonly abbreviated 'SOP'.)

classes.label: article
classes.definition: The realization of a piece of writing on a particular topic, usually published within a periodical publication (e.g. journal, magazine and newspaper).
classes.comment: The realization of a piece of writing on a particular topic, usually published within a periodical publication (e.g. journal, magazine and newspaper).

classes.label: digital item
classes.definition: A digital object, such as a computer file.
classes.comment: A digital object, such as a computer file. | A digital item is an exemplar of a digital manifestation only and it is always stored in a storage medium suitable for digital objects, such as CDs, DVDs, HDs and the Web.

classes.label: wikipedia entry
classes.definition: Information about a particular topic in one of the versions of Wikipedia, the online encyclopedia (http://www.wikipedia.org/).
classes.comment: Information about a particular topic in one of the versions of Wikipedia, the online encyclopedia (http://www.wikipedia.org/).

classes.label: e-mail
classes.definition: A message transmitted over the internet as an item of electronic mail, typically based on the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).  Emails can have computer files containing documents, dataset and images attached to them or embedded within them.
classes.comment: A message transmitted over the internet as an item of electronic mail, typically based on the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).  Emails can have computer files containing documents, dataset and images attached to them or embedded within them.

classes.label: model
classes.definition: A mathematical, graphical or physical representation of some physical reality, conceptual idea or theoretical construct.
classes.comment: A mathematical, graphical or physical representation of some physical reality, conceptual idea or theoretical construct.

classes.label: archival document
classes.definition: An archival document is a realization of the content related to an archival record. It can be exemplified as a book, a document, a letter, a database, etc.
classes.comment: An archival document is a realization of the content related to an archival record. It can be exemplified as a book, a document, a letter, a database, etc.

classes.label: clinical trial report
classes.definition: The report of a pre-planned medical or veterinary clinical study of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic or prophylactic drugs, or of devices, treatments or techniques, involving a randomized controlled trial for evidence-based assessment in humans or animals selected according to predetermined criteria of eligibility and observed for evidence of favourable and unfavourable effects.
classes.comment: The report of a pre-planned medical or veterinary clinical study of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic or prophylactic drugs, or of devices, treatments or techniques, involving a randomized controlled trial for evidence-based assessment in humans or animals selected according to predetermined criteria of eligibility and observed for evidence of favourable and unfavourable effects.

classes.label: journal issue
classes.definition: A particular published issue of a journal, one or more of which will constitute a volume of the journal.
classes.comment: A particular published issue of a journal, one or more of which will constitute a volume of the journal.

classes.label: case report
classes.definition: A report about a particular case or situation.
classes.comment: A report about a particular case or situation.

classes.label: essay
classes.definition: A piece of non-fiction writing on a particular subject, usually of moderate length and without chapters.
classes.comment: A piece of non-fiction writing on a particular subject, usually of moderate length and without chapters.

classes.label: screenplay
classes.definition: A written work made especially for a film or television program. Screenplays can be original works or adaptations from existing pieces of writing, for example novels.
classes.comment: A written work made especially for a film or television program. Screenplays can be original works or adaptations from existing pieces of writing, for example novels.

classes.label: magazine issue
classes.definition: A particular published  issue of a magazine, identified by date, and sometimes also by place (e.g. 'West Coast edition') or language (e.g. 'Spanish edition').
classes.comment: A particular published  issue of a magazine, identified by date, and sometimes also by place (e.g. 'West Coast edition') or language (e.g. 'Spanish edition').

classes.label: book chapter
classes.definition: A defined chapter of a book, usually with a separate title or number.
classes.comment: A defined chapter of a book, usually with a separate title or number.

classes.label: review paper
classes.definition:
A scholarly work that surveys the state of the art of topics central to a particular subject or relating to a specific domain (e.g. the scope of a certain journal or conference). Papers of this kind may contain a selective bibliography listing key papers related to the subject or providing advice on information sources, or they may strive to be comprehensive, covering all contributions to the development of a topic and exploring their different findings or views.

E.g. see http://www.emeraldgrouppublishing.com/products/journals/author_guidelines.htm?id=JD

classes.label: literary artistic work
classes.definition: A literary creative work, such as a novel, play, poem or song.
classes.comment: A literary creative work, such as a novel, play, poem or song.

classes.label: bachelor's thesis
classes.definition: A thesis reporting a research project undertaken as part of an undergraduate course of education leading to a bachelor's degree.
classes.comment: A thesis reporting a research project undertaken as part of an undergraduate course of education leading to a bachelor's degree.

classes.label: subject term
classes.definition: A concept that defines a term within the controlled vocabulary of a particular classification system, such as the ACM Computing Classification System or MeSH, the Medical Subject Headings, used as an annotation to describe the subject, meaning or content of an entity.
classes.comment: A concept that defines a term within the controlled vocabulary of a particular classification system, such as the ACM Computing Classification System or MeSH, the Medical Subject Headings, used as an annotation to describe the subject, meaning or content of an entity.

classes.label: resource paper
classes.definition:
A scholarly work that describes resources developed to provide experimental materials or facilities, support a research hypothesis, to provide answers to a research question, or that have contributed to the generation of novel scientific work. Examples of such resources include, for experimental sciences, mouse mutant lines and large communally used X-ray or neutron sources, and, for computer sciences, datasets, ontologies, vocabularies, ontology design patterns, evaluation benchmarks or methods, services, APIs and software frameworks, workflows, crowdsourcing task designs, protocols and metrics.

E.g. see http://iswc2018.semanticweb.org/call-for-resources-track-papers/

classes.label: digital storage medium
classes.definition: A means of storing information in digital form, involving binary encoding of data in 0s and 1s, e.g. a computer random access memory, hard disc, USB stick, CD, DVD or digital magnetic tape.
classes.comment: A means of storing information in digital form, involving binary encoding of data in 0s and 1s, e.g. a computer random access memory, hard disc, USB stick, CD, DVD or digital magnetic tape.

classes.label: structured summary
classes.definition: A structured summary containing essential metadata describing a research investigation and/or the research outputs that have resulted from it, for example datasets and journal articles, structured according to some minimal information standard.  Such a structured summary can be embodied in both human-readable and machine-readable manifestations, e.g. HTML and RDF.  Such a structured summary differs from the Abstract of a journal article, in that the latter is written as a piece of continuous prose, but typically omits vital factual information about the investigation, such as when and where it was conducted, by whom, and on now many specimens or subjects.
classes.comment: A structured summary containing essential metadata describing a research investigation and/or the research outputs that have resulted from it, for example datasets and journal articles, structured according to some minimal information standard.  Such a structured summary can be embodied in both human-readable and machine-readable manifestations, e.g. HTML and RDF.  Such a structured summary differs from the Abstract of a journal article, in that the latter is written as a piece of continuous prose, but typically omits vital factual information about the investigation, such as when and where it was conducted, by whom, and on now many specimens or subjects.

classes.label: data management plan
classes.definition: A structured document giving information about how data arising from a research project or other endeavour is to be manages, preserved and shared.
classes.comment: A structured document giving information about how data arising from a research project or other endeavour is to be manages, preserved and shared.

classes.label: poem
classes.definition: An artistic work written with an intensity or beauty of language more characteristic of poetry than of prose.
classes.comment: An artistic work written with an intensity or beauty of language more characteristic of poetry than of prose.

classes.label: proceedings paper
classes.definition: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually published within an academic proceedings volume.
classes.comment: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually published within an academic proceedings volume.

classes.label: newspaper editorial
classes.definition: An editorial published in an issue of a newspaper.
classes.comment: An editorial published in an issue of a newspaper.

classes.label: directory
classes.definition: A database of information which is heavily optimized for reading.
classes.comment: A database of information which is heavily optimized for reading.

classes.label: table of contents
classes.definition: A table listing the parts of publication such as a book or technical specification, and the pages on which these content elements start (if the publication is printed or otherwise organized into pages), usually listed in order of appearance.  The Table of Contents typically includes first-level headers, such as the chapter titles of a book, and may also include second- and even third-level headers.  In electronic works, the Table of Contents entries are often internally hyperlinked to the content items, so that clicking on the entry takes the reader to that item.
classes.comment: A table listing the parts of publication such as a book or technical specification, and the pages on which these content elements start (if the publication is printed or otherwise organized into pages), usually listed in order of appearance.  The Table of Contents typically includes first-level headers, such as the chapter titles of a book, and may also include second- and even third-level headers.  In electronic works, the Table of Contents entries are often internally hyperlinked to the content items, so that clicking on the entry takes the reader to that item.

classes.label: computer file
classes.definition: A digital item containing information in computer-readable form encoded in a particular format.
classes.comment: A digital item containing information in computer-readable form encoded in a particular format.

classes.label: erratum
classes.definition: A formal correction to an error introduced by the publisher into a previously published document.
classes.comment: A formal correction to an error introduced by the publisher into a previously published document.

classes.label: analog manifestation
classes.definition: A manifestation in an analog form.
classes.comment: A manifestation in an analog form.

classes.label: image
classes.definition: A visual representation other than text, including all types of moving image and still image.
classes.comment: A visual representation other than text, including all types of moving image and still image.

classes.label: textbook
classes.definition: A book containing instructional material relating to a particular topic of academic study, designed to be read by students.
classes.comment: A book containing instructional material relating to a particular topic of academic study, designed to be read by students.

classes.label: examination paper
classes.definition: A set of questions on a particular topic designed to test the academic, professional or technical ability of the person taking the examination, with achievement of a pass grade in the examination typically being a prerequisite for the award of an educational award such as a degree, or of a professional or technical qualification.
classes.comment: A set of questions on a particular topic designed to test the academic, professional or technical ability of the person taking the examination, with achievement of a pass grade in the examination typically being a prerequisite for the award of an educational award such as a degree, or of a professional or technical qualification.

classes.label: retraction notice
classes.definition: The realization of a retraction. A formal document which publicly withdraws, cancels, refutes, reverses an earlier statement or publication or announces the act of desisting from publishing the original statement.
classes.comment: The realization of a retraction. A formal document which publicly withdraws, cancels, refutes, reverses an earlier statement or publication or announces the act of desisting from publishing the original statement.

classes.label: grant application
classes.definition: A formal written request for financial support from a grant-giving body in support of a project, for example an academic research project.  (See also fabio:CaseForSupport.)
classes.comment: A formal written request for financial support from a grant-giving body in support of a project, for example an academic research project.  (See also fabio:CaseForSupport.)

classes.label: editorial
classes.definition: The realization of an opinion written by an editor.
classes.comment: The realization of an opinion written by an editor.

classes.label: case for support document
classes.definition: A document containing the case for support for a particular project, usually contained within a grant application document but sometimes distributed separately, without the financial and organizational information that the grant application document also contains.
classes.comment: A document containing the case for support for a particular project, usually contained within a grant application document but sometimes distributed separately, without the financial and organizational information that the grant application document also contains.

classes.label: work package
classes.definition: A component of the case for support of a grant application, describing a particular aspect of the work to be undertaken.
classes.comment: A component of the case for support of a grant application, describing a particular aspect of the work to be undertaken.

classes.label: song
classes.definition: A musical composition that contains vocal parts ('lyrics') that are performed ('sung').
classes.comment: A musical composition that contains vocal parts ('lyrics') that are performed ('sung').

classes.label: opinion
classes.definition: An expression of a personal or professional opinion on an issue or topic.
classes.comment: An expression of a personal or professional opinion on an issue or topic.

classes.label: critical edition
classes.definition: A new edition of a historical publication, edited by a scholar other than the original author, containing within the body text the supposedly best version of the original work, with footnotes detailing and commenting on textual variations between different versions, typically with an introduction to the original work written by the scholar, and with a bibliography listing related publications.
classes.comment: A new edition of a historical publication, edited by a scholar other than the original author, containing within the body text the supposedly best version of the original work, with footnotes detailing and commenting on textual variations between different versions, typically with an introduction to the original work written by the scholar, and with a bibliography listing related publications.

classes.label: metadata document
classes.definition: A document that contains metadata information describing one or more characteristics of an entity.
classes.comment: A document that contains metadata information describing one or more characteristics of an entity.

classes.label: addendum
classes.definition: An item of material added at the end of a book or other publication, typically to include omitted or late-arriving material.
classes.comment: An item of material added at the end of a book or other publication, typically to include omitted or late-arriving material.

classes.label: letter
classes.definition: A written or printed communication of a personal or professional nature between individuals and/or representatives of corporate bodies, usually transmitted by the postal service or published in a periodical.  In the latter case, the letter is typically addressed to the editor and comments on or discussed an item previously published by that periodical, or of interest to its readership.
classes.comment: A written or printed communication of a personal or professional nature between individuals and/or representatives of corporate bodies, usually transmitted by the postal service or published in a periodical.  In the latter case, the letter is typically addressed to the editor and comments on or discussed an item previously published by that periodical, or of interest to its readership.

classes.label: report document
classes.definition: The realization of a report, usually in printed form.
classes.comment: The realization of a report, usually in printed form.

classes.label: vocabulary mapping document
classes.definition: A document containing a vocabulary mapping
classes.comment: A document containing a vocabulary mapping

classes.label: academic proceedings
classes.definition: A document containing the programme and collected papers, or their abstracts, presented at an academic meeting.
classes.comment: A document containing the programme and collected papers, or their abstracts, presented at an academic meeting.

classes.label: magazine article
classes.definition: An article published in a magazine issue.
classes.comment: An article published in a magazine issue.

classes.label: instructional work
classes.definition: A work created for the purpose of education or instruction, that may be expressed as a  text book, a lecture, a tutorial or an instruction manual.
classes.comment: A work created for the purpose of education or instruction, that may be expressed as a  text book, a lecture, a tutorial or an instruction manual.

classes.label: timetable
classes.definition: A tabular dataset providing information about the times and locations of a planned series of events.
classes.comment: A tabular dataset providing information about the times and locations of a planned series of events.

classes.label: item collection
classes.definition: A collection of items.
classes.comment: A collection of items.

classes.label: position paper
classes.definition:
A scholarly work that reports a particular intellectual position or viewpoint regarding a particular scholarly topic. Usually, these papers are dependent on the author's opinion or interpretation, do not have an evaluation, and need to present relevant and novel discussion points in a thorough manner.

E.g. see https://datasciencehub.net/content/guidelines-authors
classes.comment:
A scholarly work that reports a particular intellectual position or viewpoint regarding a particular scholarly topic. Usually, these papers are dependent on the author's opinion or interpretation, do not have an evaluation, and need to present relevant and novel discussion points in a thorough manner.

E.g. see https://datasciencehub.net/content/guidelines-authors

classes.label: technical standard
classes.definition: An official or public specification of, or requirement for, a technical method, practice, process or protocol that is involved in, for example, manufacturing, computation, electronic communication, or digital media.
classes.comment: An official or public specification of, or requirement for, a technical method, practice, process or protocol that is involved in, for example, manufacturing, computation, electronic communication, or digital media.

classes.label: personal communication
classes.definition: Information communicated personally by verbal or written means from one individual to one or more another persons or organizations.
classes.comment: Information communicated personally by verbal or written means from one individual to one or more another persons or organizations.

classes.label: proof
classes.definition: In printing and publishing, a proof copy is the preliminary version of a publication, after the inclusion of any author corrections following review, and after copy editing and formatting to bring the manuscript into the house style, intended for final checking prior to publication to detect and eliminate typographical errors, omissions or transpositions of text, incorrect layout or placement of illustrations and tables, or other formatting errors.  Those who check proofs include the editor, possibly the peer-reviewers (to ensure that their requested modifications have been included to their satisfaction), possibly an in-house professional proof-reader, and / or the author, who is ultimately responsible for ensuring the published work says what (s)he means it to say.  Substantive changes to the text are not permitted once the manuscript has reached proof stage.
classes.comment: In printing and publishing, a proof copy is the preliminary version of a publication, after the inclusion of any author corrections following review, and after copy editing and formatting to bring the manuscript into the house style, intended for final checking prior to publication to detect and eliminate typographical errors, omissions or transpositions of text, incorrect layout or placement of illustrations and tables, or other formatting errors.  Those who check proofs include the editor, possibly the peer-reviewers (to ensure that their requested modifications have been included to their satisfaction), possibly an in-house professional proof-reader, and / or the author, who is ultimately responsible for ensuring the published work says what (s)he means it to say.  Substantive changes to the text are not permitted once the manuscript has reached proof stage.

classes.label: workflow
classes.definition: A recorded sequence of connected steps, which may be automated, specifying a reliably repeatable sequence of operations to be undertaken when conducting a particular job, for example an in silico investigation that extracts and processes information from a number of bioinformatics databases.
classes.comment: A recorded sequence of connected steps, which may be automated, specifying a reliably repeatable sequence of operations to be undertaken when conducting a particular job, for example an in silico investigation that extracts and processes information from a number of bioinformatics databases.

classes.label: notebook
classes.definition: A book containing personal notes, typically created by writing into a physical book with blank pages.
classes.comment: A book containing personal notes, typically created by writing into a physical book with blank pages.

classes.label: figure
classes.definition: A visual communication object comprising one or more still images on a related theme.  If included within a publication, a figure is typically unaligned with the main body of text, having its own descriptive textual figure legend.
classes.comment: A visual communication object comprising one or more still images on a related theme.  If included within a publication, a figure is typically unaligned with the main body of text, having its own descriptive textual figure legend.

classes.label: periodical item
classes.definition: A piece of writing published in a periodical issue, typically accompanied by other items by different authors.
classes.comment: A piece of writing published in a periodical issue, typically accompanied by other items by different authors.

classes.label: folksonomy
classes.definition: A system of classification derived from the practice and method of collaboratively creating and managing tags to annotate and categorize content in a particular domain. [Contrast fabio:Ontology]
classes.comment: A system of classification derived from the practice and method of collaboratively creating and managing tags to annotate and categorize content in a particular domain. [Contrast fabio:Ontology]

classes.label: poster paper
classes.definition: A paper that typically accompanies a poster describing some preliminary  results of research, usually presented during a conference or a workshop.
classes.comment: A paper that typically accompanies a poster describing some preliminary  results of research, usually presented during a conference or a workshop.

classes.label: spreadsheet
classes.definition: An electronic form of data storage that displays a grid of rows and columns, in which each editable cell can contain alphanumeric text, a numeric value, or a formula that defines how the content of that cell is to be calculated from the content of another cell or cells.
classes.comment: An electronic form of data storage that displays a grid of rows and columns, in which each editable cell can contain alphanumeric text, a numeric value, or a formula that defines how the content of that cell is to be calculated from the content of another cell or cells.

classes.label: project plan
classes.definition: A document used to guide project planning, execution and control, specifying the project's goal and objectives and the activities and resources required to achieve these, setting out the project schedule, and identifying the major workpackages, milestones and deliverables.  A project plan will typically contain a Gantt chart.
classes.comment: A document used to guide project planning, execution and control, specifying the project's goal and objectives and the activities and resources required to achieve these, setting out the project schedule, and identifying the major workpackages, milestones and deliverables.  A project plan will typically contain a Gantt chart.

classes.label: journal
classes.definition: A scholarly periodical primarily devoted to the publication of original research papers. [Printed and electronic manifestations of the same journal are usually identified by separate print and electronic International Standard Serial Numbers (ISSN or eISSN, respectively), that identifies the journal as a whole, not to individual issues of it.]
classes.comment: A scholarly periodical primarily devoted to the publication of original research papers. [Printed and electronic manifestations of the same journal are usually identified by separate print and electronic International Standard Serial Numbers (ISSN or eISSN, respectively), that identifies the journal as a whole, not to individual issues of it.]

classes.label: working paper
classes.definition: An unpublished paper, usually circulated privately among a small group of peers, to provide information or with a request for comments or editorial improvement.
classes.comment: An unpublished paper, usually circulated privately among a small group of peers, to provide information or with a request for comments or editorial improvement.

classes.label: master's thesis
classes.definition: A thesis reporting a research project undertaken as part of a graduate course of education leading to a master's degree.
classes.comment: A thesis reporting a research project undertaken as part of a graduate course of education leading to a master's degree.

classes.label: cover
classes.definition: A protective covering used to bind together the pages of a document or the first, informative, page of a digital document.
classes.comment: A protective covering used to bind together the pages of a document or the first, informative, page of a digital document.

classes.label: journal article
classes.definition: An article, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, published in a journal issue.
classes.comment: An article, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, published in a journal issue.

classes.label: deliverable report
classes.definition: A report describing the outcomes of specific project, typically listing 'deliverables' created or 'milestones' achieved during the project.
classes.comment: A report describing the outcomes of specific project, typically listing 'deliverables' created or 'milestones' achieved during the project.

classes.label: demo paper
classes.definition: A demonstration paper, typically describing a new product, service or system created as a result of research, usually presented during a conference or workshop.
classes.comment: A demonstration paper, typically describing a new product, service or system created as a result of research, usually presented during a conference or workshop.

classes.label: dust jacket
classes.definition: A detachable outer cover, usually made of paper and printed with text and illustrations. This outer cover has folded flaps that hold it to the cover of a document.
classes.comment: A detachable outer cover, usually made of paper and printed with text and illustrations. This outer cover has folded flaps that hold it to the cover of a document.

classes.label: review
classes.definition: A review of others' work.
classes.comment: A review of others' work.

classes.label: specification
classes.definition: An explicit description of, or set of requirements to be satisfied by, a material, product, resource, service or standard.
classes.comment: An explicit description of, or set of requirements to be satisfied by, a material, product, resource, service or standard.

classes.label: legal opinion
classes.definition: A written explanation by a judge or group of judges that accompanies a ruling in a legal case, laying out the reasons and legal principles for the ruling, and sometimes containing pronouncements about what the law is and how it should be interpreted.
classes.comment: A written explanation by a judge or group of judges that accompanies a ruling in a legal case, laying out the reasons and legal principles for the ruling, and sometimes containing pronouncements about what the law is and how it should be interpreted.

classes.label: magazine
classes.definition: A periodical, usually devoted to a particular topic or domain of interest, and usually published weekly or monthly, consisting primarily of  non-peer reviewed editorials, journalistic news items and more substantive articles, reviews, book reviews and discussions concerning current or recent events and publications, and matters of interest to the domain served by the magazine.  [Some scientific journals, notably Science and Nature, also secondarily serve as science magazines by containing substantive editorials and news items on vital or controversial issues].
classes.comment: A periodical, usually devoted to a particular topic or domain of interest, and usually published weekly or monthly, consisting primarily of  non-peer reviewed editorials, journalistic news items and more substantive articles, reviews, book reviews and discussions concerning current or recent events and publications, and matters of interest to the domain served by the magazine.  [Some scientific journals, notably Science and Nature, also secondarily serve as science magazines by containing substantive editorials and news items on vital or controversial issues].

classes.label: questionnaire
classes.definition: A set of questions on a particular topic, usually in the form of multiple choice questions requiring the respondent to select the correct answer, or providing the ability to indicate support for or against a proposal on a numerical scale, designed for rapid numerical analysis of responses and often used in surveying public opinion.
classes.comment: A set of questions on a particular topic, usually in the form of multiple choice questions requiring the respondent to select the correct answer, or providing the ability to indicate support for or against a proposal on a numerical scale, designed for rapid numerical analysis of responses and often used in surveying public opinion.

classes.label: web page
classes.definition: A Web manifestation usually identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), and made accessible to a user by means of the Hypertext Transport Protocol (HTTP) in a Web browser window. Several interlinked web pages hosted together on a Web server and accessed through a single domain name or IP address constitute a web site.
classes.comment: A Web manifestation usually identified by a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), and made accessible to a user by means of the Hypertext Transport Protocol (HTTP) in a Web browser window. Several interlinked web pages hosted together on a Web server and accessed through a single domain name or IP address constitute a web site.

classes.label: Gantt chart
classes.definition: A horizontal bar chart used to guide project planning, execution and control, illustrating the project schedule, with a separate line indicating the start and end dates of each of the key project activities or workpackages, and optionally showing the dependencies between these items. A Gantt chart is typically part of a project plan.
classes.comment: A horizontal bar chart used to guide project planning, execution and control, illustrating the project schedule, with a separate line indicating the start and end dates of each of the key project activities or workpackages, and optionally showing the dependencies between these items. A Gantt chart is typically part of a project plan.

classes.label: hardback
classes.definition: A print object bound with rigid protective covers (typically of cardboard covered with cloth, heavy paper, or sometimes leather).
classes.comment: A print object bound with rigid protective covers (typically of cardboard covered with cloth, heavy paper, or sometimes leather).

classes.label: conference poster
classes.definition: A display poster, typically containing text with illustrative figures and/or tables, usually reporting research results or proposing hypotheses, submitted for acceptance to and/or presented at a conference, seminar, symposium, workshop or similar event.
classes.comment: A display poster, typically containing text with illustrative figures and/or tables, usually reporting research results or proposing hypotheses, submitted for acceptance to and/or presented at a conference, seminar, symposium, workshop or similar event.

classes.label: policy document
classes.definition: A document embodying a policy that descibes and defines how something should be done.
classes.comment: A document embodying a policy that descibes and defines how something should be done.

classes.label: library catalog
classes.definition: The catalog of the holdings of a library, for example that of the Library of Congress (http://catalog.loc.gov/).
classes.comment: The catalog of the holdings of a library, for example that of the Library of Congress (http://catalog.loc.gov/).

classes.label: executive summary
classes.definition: An executive summary is a brief report summarizing a longer formal report, designed to present the key points, conclusions and recommendations arising from the study being reported, for readers too busy to take the time to read the complete report.
classes.comment: An executive summary is a brief report summarizing a longer formal report, designed to present the key points, conclusions and recommendations arising from the study being reported, for readers too busy to take the time to read the complete report.

classes.label: newspaper issue
classes.definition: A particular published  issue of a newspaper, identified by date, and sometimes also by place or time (e.g. 'Late London Edition').
classes.comment: A particular published  issue of a newspaper, identified by date, and sometimes also by place or time (e.g. 'Late London Edition').

classes.label: blog post
classes.definition: Information manifested in a blog, one of a set of periodic sequential entries containing commentary, descriptions of events, or other material such as images or videos, usually displayed in reverse-chronological order and usually maintained by an individual, or comments on such a post.
classes.comment: Information manifested in a blog, one of a set of periodic sequential entries containing commentary, descriptions of events, or other material such as images or videos, usually displayed in reverse-chronological order and usually maintained by an individual, or comments on such a post.

classes.label: workshop paper
classes.definition: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually presented at a workshop and published within a workshop proceedings volume.
classes.comment: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually presented at a workshop and published within a workshop proceedings volume.

classes.label: clinical guideline
classes.definition: A recommendation on the appropriate treatment and care of people with a specific disease or condition, based on the best available evidence, designed to help healthcare professionals in their work.
classes.comment: A recommendation on the appropriate treatment and care of people with a specific disease or condition, based on the best available evidence, designed to help healthcare professionals in their work.

classes.label: abstract
classes.definition: A brief summary of a work on a particular subject, designed to act as the point-of-entry that will help the reader quickly to obtain an overview of the work's contents.   The abstract may be an integral part of the work itself, written by the same author(s) and appearing at the beginning of a work such as a research paper, report, review or thesis.  Alternatively it may be separate from the published work itself, and written by someone other than the author(s) of the published work, for example by a member of a professional abstracting service such as CAB Abstracts.
classes.comment: A brief summary of a work on a particular subject, designed to act as the point-of-entry that will help the reader quickly to obtain an overview of the work's contents.   The abstract may be an integral part of the work itself, written by the same author(s) and appearing at the beginning of a work such as a research paper, report, review or thesis.  Alternatively it may be separate from the published work itself, and written by someone other than the author(s) of the published work, for example by a member of a professional abstracting service such as CAB Abstracts.

classes.label: book series
classes.definition: A sequence of books having certain characteristics in common that are formally identified together as a group - for instance, the books in the Law, Governance and Technology Series published by Springer.
classes.comment: A sequence of books having certain characteristics in common that are formally identified together as a group - for instance, the books in the Law, Governance and Technology Series published by Springer.

classes.label: computer application
classes.definition: A computer program designed to assist a human user to perform one or more goal-oriented tasks such as word processing or image processing.  A computer application will typically save its output files in one or more specific formats, conforming either to proprietary or open standards.
classes.comment: A computer program designed to assist a human user to perform one or more goal-oriented tasks such as word processing or image processing.  A computer application will typically save its output files in one or more specific formats, conforming either to proprietary or open standards.

classes.label: vocabulary document
classes.definition: A document containing a vocabulary
classes.comment: A document containing a vocabulary

classes.label: API
classes.definition: A computer program that enables a separate computer to interact programmatically with the computer running the API.  (Commonly abbreviated 'API'.)
classes.comment: A computer program that enables a separate computer to interact programmatically with the computer running the API.  (Commonly abbreviated 'API'.)

classes.label: periodical issue
classes.definition: A particular issue of a periodical, identified and distinguished from other issues of the same publication by date and/or issue number and/or volume number, and comprising separate periodical items such as editorials, articles and news items.
classes.comment: A particular issue of a periodical, identified and distinguished from other issues of the same publication by date and/or issue number and/or volume number, and comprising separate periodical items such as editorials, articles and news items.

classes.label: database
classes.definition: A structured collection of logically related records or data usually stored and retrieved using computer-based means.
classes.comment: A structured collection of logically related records or data usually stored and retrieved using computer-based means.

classes.label: discipline dictionary
classes.definition: A discipline dictionary is a collection of subject disciplines.
classes.comment: A discipline dictionary is a collection of subject disciplines.

classes.label: research paper
classes.definition:
A scholarly work that reports original research contributions addressing theoretical, analytical or experimental aspects of a particular scholarly domain.

E.g. see http://iswc2018.semanticweb.org/call-for-research-track-papers/.
classes.comment:
A scholarly work that reports original research contributions addressing theoretical, analytical or experimental aspects of a particular scholarly domain.

E.g. see http://iswc2018.semanticweb.org/call-for-research-track-papers/.

classes.label: clinical case report
classes.definition: A presentation of findings following a clinical or medical investigation on a human or animal patient, that may contain a diagnosis and proposals for therapeutic treatment and/or epidemiological control measures, or may propose further evaluative studies that will eventually lead to such outcomes.
classes.comment: A presentation of findings following a clinical or medical investigation on a human or animal patient, that may contain a diagnosis and proposals for therapeutic treatment and/or epidemiological control measures, or may propose further evaluative studies that will eventually lead to such outcomes.

classes.label: review article
classes.definition: An article that contains a review.
classes.comment: An article that contains a review.

classes.label: series
classes.definition: A sequence of expressions having certain characteristics in common that are formally identified together as a group.
classes.comment: A sequence of expressions having certain characteristics in common that are formally identified together as a group.

classes.label: uncontrolled vocabulary
classes.definition: A non-defined collection of words and phrases relating to a particular domain of knowledge, usually added freely by a community, in which homonyms, synonyms and similar ambiguities of meaning present in natural language are not formally disambiguated.
classes.comment: A non-defined collection of words and phrases relating to a particular domain of knowledge, usually added freely by a community, in which homonyms, synonyms and similar ambiguities of meaning present in natural language are not formally disambiguated.

classes.label: technical report
classes.definition: A report of a technical nature.
classes.comment: A report of a technical nature.

classes.label: comment
classes.definition: A verbal or written remark concerning some entity.  In written form, a comment is often appended to that entity and termed an annotation.  Within computer programs or ontologies, comments are added to enhance human understanding, and are usually prefaced by a special syntactic symbol that ensures they are ignored during execution of the program.
classes.comment: A verbal or written remark concerning some entity.  In written form, a comment is often appended to that entity and termed an annotation.  Within computer programs or ontologies, comments are added to enhance human understanding, and are usually prefaced by a special syntactic symbol that ensures they are ignored during execution of the program.

classes.label: conference paper
classes.definition: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually published within a conference proceedings volume.
classes.comment: A paper, typically the realization of a research paper reporting original research findings, usually published within a conference proceedings volume.

classes.label: presentation
classes.definition: A set of slides containing text, tables or figures, designed to communicate ideas or research results, for projection and viewing by an audience at a conference, symposium, seminar, lecture, workshop or other gatherings, typically embodied in a particular manifestation format such as a SlideShare or PowerPoint slideshow.
classes.comment: A set of slides containing text, tables or figures, designed to communicate ideas or research results, for projection and viewing by an audience at a conference, symposium, seminar, lecture, workshop or other gatherings, typically embodied in a particular manifestation format such as a SlideShare or PowerPoint slideshow.

classes.label: excerpt
classes.definition:
A segment or passage selected from a larger expression for use in another expression, usually with specific attribution to its original source.

[Note: Use fabio:Excerpt to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is not a passage of speech, and fabio:Quotation to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is a passage of speech.]
classes.comment:
A segment or passage selected from a larger expression for use in another expression, usually with specific attribution to its original source.

[Note: Use fabio:Excerpt to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is not a passage of speech, and fabio:Quotation to indicate a segment or passage selected from another expression that is a passage of speech.] | An excerpt is more general than a quotation, and is generally used to indicate a re-published extract from a book, instruction manual, film, radio programme, etc, that need not be what someone said.  

For example:
     Oxford    01865
     Oxshott   01372
     Oxted      01883
     Oxton      01578
is an excerpt from the UK Dialling Codes section of the Oxford Telephone Directory.  

Similarly, the following concluding passage from William Wordsworth's poem Lines written a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey is an excerpt rather than a quotation:
                                           Nor wilt thou then forget,    
    That after many wanderings, many years    
    Of absence, these steep woods and lofty cliffs,    
    And this green pastoral landscape, were to me    
    More dear, both for themselves and for thy sake.

classes.label: archival document set
classes.definition: A collection of archival document.
classes.comment: A collection of archival document.

classes.label: methods paper
classes.definition: A scholarly work detailing a method, procedure or experimental protocol employed in a particular scholarly domain.
classes.comment: A scholarly work detailing a method, procedure or experimental protocol employed in a particular scholarly domain.

classes.label: collected works
classes.definition: A collection of the literary or scholastic works of a single person.
classes.comment: A collection of the literary or scholastic works of a single person.

classes.label: musical composition
classes.definition: A piece of music, typically in the form of a composition recorded in musical notation.
classes.comment: A piece of music, typically in the form of a composition recorded in musical notation.

classes.label: postprint
classes.definition: The version of an author's original scholarly work, such as a research paper or a review, re-submitted for publication after revision by the author in the light of comments from reviewers.  [Note: For the version before peer review, use fabio:Preprint. For the final piblished version, use fabio:DefinitiveVersion.]
classes.comment: The version of an author's original scholarly work, such as a research paper or a review, re-submitted for publication after revision by the author in the light of comments from reviewers.  [Note: For the version before peer review, use fabio:Preprint. For the final piblished version, use fabio:DefinitiveVersion.]

classes.label: bibliographic database
classes.definition: A database providing an authoritative source of bibliographic information, for example PubMed (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed), CrossRef Metadata Search (http://search.crossref.org/) and PubMed Central (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/).
classes.comment: A database providing an authoritative source of bibliographic information, for example PubMed (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed), CrossRef Metadata Search (http://search.crossref.org/) and PubMed Central (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/).

classes.label: catalog
classes.definition: A list of items describing the content of a resource, for example items in an exhibition, items offered for sale by a vendor, or entities contained within a library or collection.  Ideally, catalogs are created according to specific and uniform principles of construction and are under the control of an authority file.
classes.comment: A list of items describing the content of a resource, for example items in an exhibition, items offered for sale by a vendor, or entities contained within a library or collection.  Ideally, catalogs are created according to specific and uniform principles of construction and are under the control of an authority file.

classes.label: manifestation
classes.definition:
A subclass of FRBR manifestation, restricted to manifestations of fabio:Expressions. fabio:Manifestation specifically applies to electronic (digital) as well as to physical manifestations of expressions.  

Examples of different manifestations of a single 'version of record' expression of a scholarly work include an article in a print journal or the on-line version of that article as a web page.
classes.comment:
A subclass of FRBR manifestation, restricted to manifestations of fabio:Expressions. fabio:Manifestation specifically applies to electronic (digital) as well as to physical manifestations of expressions.  

Examples of different manifestations of a single 'version of record' expression of a scholarly work include an article in a print journal or the on-line version of that article as a web page. | A fabio:Manifestation can only have part or be part of another fabio:Manifestation.  Moreover, it can be an embodiment only of a fabio:Expression and it can be exemplified only by fabio:Item(s).

classes.label: news report
classes.definition: A report of an item of news.
classes.comment: A report of an item of news.

classes.label: specification document
classes.definition: The realization of a specification (a standard, a workflow, etc.).
classes.comment: The realization of a specification (a standard, a workflow, etc.).

classes.label: announcement
classes.definition: A formal statement about something.
classes.comment: A formal statement about something.

classes.label: still image
classes.definition: A recorded static visual representation. This class of image includes diagrams, drawings, graphs, graphic designs, plans, maps, photographs and prints.
classes.comment: A recorded static visual representation. This class of image includes diagrams, drawings, graphs, graphic designs, plans, maps, photographs and prints.

classes.label: Ph.D. symposium paper
classes.definition: A paper, usually presented during a specific session of a conference dedicated to Ph.D. students, that describes ongoing Ph.D. student's research.
classes.comment: A paper, usually presented during a specific session of a conference dedicated to Ph.D. students, that describes ongoing Ph.D. student's research.

classes.label: workshop proceedings
